newsitem.title: POLAND: Row unlikely to cause early Polish polls-president.
newsitem.headline: Row unlikely to cause early Polish polls-president.

text.p: A row between Poland's two ruling parties over the dismissal of a minister is unlikely to cause a breakdown in the coalition and early elections, President Aleksander Kwasniewski said on Thursday.

Kwasniewski on Wednesday signed the dismissal of Foreign Trade Minister Jacek Buchacz, from the smaller Peasant party (PSL), on a motion from the prime minister who belongs to the dominant, ex-communist Democratic Left Alliance (SLD). @

"I believe that Prime Minister Wlodzimierz Cimoszewicz, a sensible man, and the leadership of the PSL and SLD who are also responsible people, will find a solution in this matter," PAP news agency quoted Kwasniewski as telling reporters.
The sudden dismissal of Buchacz aroused the fury of PSL leaders who said it was an SLD provocation which might force them to quit the government.
This would lead to early elections, otherwise not scheduled until September 1997, in spring next year. @
Kwasniewski said early polls were very unlikely as it was doubtful the necessary two-thirds majority of parliamentary deputies would support such an outcome, PAP reported.

A government statement on Wednesday said Buchacz had been fired after official probes revealed that the treasury had been involved in ventures concerning export guarantees, in which the distinction between public and private property was unclear.
Kwasniewski, the SLD's former leader, said he had signed the dismissal of Buchacz after being clearly shown that it was for concrete reasons rather than out of a political manoeuvre.
